description: Hey! I’m Ajmal, a UCalgary CS student interested in robotics, AI, and embedded systems. I want to build an innovative, interactive NASA Space Apps project using real data. I’m looking for collaborative teammates skilled in Python, web development, AI/ML, data visualization, UI/UX, or research. NASA API or geospatial experience is a bonus, but enthusiasm and teamwork matter most. Let’s build something awesome!
summary: SouthPoint is an interactive lunar landing-site exploration tool built for NASA’s Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. It helps users compare candidate locations and dates by visualizing sunlight and shadow, Sun and Earth visibility, terrain profiles, and planning indicators across 2D maps, cross-sections, and a 3D terrain view. Users can explore a site catalog, enter custom coordinates, and compare how illumination and communication opportunities change over time. The app combines lunar imagery and elevation layers from NASA Moon Trek with ephemeris data from JPL Horizons and an offline DE421 fallback. When a local LOLA DEM is unavailable, some terrain visuals use clearly labeled synthetic relief. Results are exploratory and are not validated landing-safety or navigation recommendations.
details: SouthPoint is a browser-based exploration tool. Users can select a catalog site, enter coordinates, choose a date and time, and explore lunar lighting, Sun/Earth visibility, terrain profiles, and site comparisons in 2D, cross-section, and 3D views. The frontend uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js/React Three Fiber, Recharts, and Zustand; the backend uses Python, FastAPI, and Skyfield. NASA Moon Trek provides lunar map layers, and JPL Horizons supplies ephemerides when available, with DE421 used as an offline fallback. Terrain capabilities depend on data availability: a local LOLA DEM can provide real elevation data, while the labeled synthetic fallback is illustrative. Some catalog coordinates are unverified, so the app is for educational exploration—not operational landing decisions.
